title: So he's a teacher!
goal: Say what you have just found out or heard with eken, and recognize how folk tales begin.

intro.text: *eken*, a separate word after a noun or adjective, marks what you have just found out or heard: *Ol mugallym eken* (So he's a teacher; he's a teacher, I'm told). Folk tales begin *Bir bar eken, bir ýok eken*: once upon a time.

vocab.en: it turns out; so; I hear (after a noun or adjective)

exercises.question: You have just found out that Merdan is a doctor. What do you say?

why.1: *Merdan lukman* states a plain fact. It doesn't say you've just learned it.

exercises.explain: *eken* marks something you've just found out: *Merdan lukman eken*, so Merdan is a doctor.

accept: This book is interesting, it turns out.
So this book is interesting.
This book turns out to be interesting.
This book is interesting, I see.
This book is interesting.

exercises.en: There's a café here, I see.

accept: eken

exercises.explain: *bar eken*: there is one, as you've just discovered.

exercises.prompt: Merdan isn't at home, it turns out.
accept: Merdan öýde ýok eken.
Merdan öýde däl eken.

reject.why: *ýokdy* says he wasn't there, as something you knew. For what you've just found out: *ýok eken*.

exercises.question: How do Turkmen folk tales usually begin?
options: Bir bar eken, bir ýok eken.

why.1: *bardy* tells what you know. The teller of a tale wasn't there, so: *bar eken*.
why.2: Not a set opening. Tales begin *Bir bar eken, bir ýok eken*.

exercises.explain: *Bir bar eken, bir ýok eken*: literally **there was one, there wasn't one**, the Turkmen **once upon a time**.

accept: Ol mugallym eken!
Mugallym eken!

exercises.prompt: In a village there was an old man. (as in a tale)
exercises.text: Bir obada bir garry adam bar eken.

accept: The fox was very clever.
The fox was very clever, they say.
The fox is very clever, it turns out.
The fox is very clever, I hear.
The fox was very clever, it turns out.

exercises.en: The king had three daughters. (in a tale)
exercises.explain: A tale is told with *eken*: *üç gyzy bar eken*, he had three daughters.

exercises.question: *Selbi kesel eken.* How does the speaker know?
options: Someone told them, or they have just found out.
They saw her yesterday and remember it.

why.1: Something you saw and remember would be the plain past: *Selbi keseldi*.
why.2: *eken* isn't about the future; it marks how you learned something.

exercises.explain: *eken* marks news: something heard or just discovered.

exercises.prompt: There's no milk at home, I see.
accept: Öýde süýt ýok eken.

reject.why: *ýokdy* is **there wasn't**, something you knew. For what you've just found: *ýok eken*.
